day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 14:00. Travel from Calgary Airport to Banff (~1.5 hrs by Brewster Express shuttle, ~$25–$30 CAD one-way). Settle into Banff Mountain Lodge and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore downtown Banff on foot – stroll Banff Avenue, visit the free Banff Visitor Centre to grab trail maps and park passes, and walk down to the Bow River Falls viewpoint (free, 10-min walk from town centre).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed walk up to the free Surprise Corner viewpoint for a stunning panoramic view of the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel and Bow River valley at golden hour. Perfect low-key first evening.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the Calgary Airport before boarding shuttle, or pick up groceries at Banff's IGA (Bear Street) upon arrival to stock up for the week (~$30–$40 CAD for staples).
meals.dinner: Nourish Bistro (Banff) – popular plant-forward café with hearty, affordable bowls and wraps; budget ~$15–$20 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Parks Canada Discovery Pass at the Visitor Centre or online before arrival (~$75 CAD/adult for an annual pass – covers all park entry fees and pays for itself within 2 days). Book the Brewster shuttle in advance to save money. Keep Day 1 light since you arrive in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Early start – Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike. Drive or take a Roam Transit bus (~$6 CAD) to Johnston Canyon trailhead (~20 min from Banff). Hike the dramatic canyon catwalk bolted into limestone cliffs to the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km). Allow 2–3 hours. Free with Parks Canada pass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue on the trail to the Ink Pots – seven vivid cold-water springs set in a meadow (~5.8 km one-way from trailhead). A hidden gem that most day visitors skip. Enjoy a packed lunch at the Ink Pots with mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff town (~4:00–5:00 PM). Relax at the hotel, then take a short walk along the Bow River Trail at dusk for wildlife spotting (elk and deer are common).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the lodge – oatmeal, fruit, and coffee from your grocery stock (~$3–$5 CAD).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the lodge – sandwiches, trail mix, and fruit. Eat at the Ink Pots viewpoint.
meals.dinner: Whitebark Café (Banff) – casual spot with soups, sandwiches, and baked goods; budget ~$12–$18 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Start by 7:30 AM to beat the crowds at Johnston Canyon – it gets very busy by mid-morning in summer. Wear sturdy shoes as the catwalk can be slippery. Total round-trip to Ink Pots is ~11.6 km with ~215 m elevation gain – moderate difficulty.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake – Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek. Depart by 6:00 AM (Moraine Lake Road is reservation-only or shuttle-required by Parks Canada in summer). Book the Parks Canada shuttle from Lake Louise Ski Area (~$8 CAD return) well in advance. Hike the Rockpile Trail (20-min loop) for the iconic Ten Peaks panorama, then walk the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return) along the impossibly blue glacial lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Valley of the Ten Peaks viewpoints along the lakeshore trail extension. Spend time photographing the turquoise water and soaring peaks. Return shuttle back to Lake Louise village by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stop briefly at Lake Louise village. Browse the small shops, then head back to Banff. Cook a simple pasta dinner at the lodge to save money after a big day out.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at the lodge before 6:00 AM departure – energy bars, bananas, and instant coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Moraine Lake shoreline – wraps, cheese, nuts, and chocolate.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the lodge – pasta with canned tomato sauce and vegetables (~$5–$8 CAD). Budget evening in.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake shuttle reservations open months in advance on the Parks Canada website – book as early as possible. This is the single most popular spot in Banff; arriving early is essential. Bring layers as mornings at 1,885 m elevation can be cool even in July. Total hiking distance ~5–7 km depending on extensions.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike & Plain of Six Glaciers. Take the early Parks Canada shuttle or drive to Lake Louise (~45 min from Banff). Walk the iconic turquoise shoreline (2 km flat lakeshore trail), then hike up to the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (~8.6 km return from the lakeshore, ~365 m elevation gain). The teahouse serves homemade baked goods and hot drinks – a classic Banff treat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Lake Louise and enjoy the views from the lakeshore. Optional: take the short Mirror Lake detour on the way back. Return to Banff by early afternoon and relax or explore the Banff Centre for Arts grounds (free, beautiful hilltop setting).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset hike up Tunnel Mountain (2.7 km return, ~300 m gain, free) – a short but rewarding hike right from town with 360° views over Banff and the Bow Valley. Perfect golden-hour spot.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the lodge – eggs, toast, and fruit.
meals.lunch: Treat yourself to tea and a scone at the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (~$8–$12 CAD) – a bucket-list Banff experience worth the splurge.
meals.dinner: Banff Ave Brewing Co. – lively pub with affordable burgers, nachos, and local craft beer; budget ~$18–$25 CAD per person including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: The Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse is hike-in only and cash/card accepted. Total hiking distance for the day can reach 12–14 km – pace yourself. Tunnel Mountain sunset hike is very accessible and takes only 45–60 minutes round-trip, ideal after a big day.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive – depart Banff by 8:00 AM and drive north on Highway 93, one of the world's most scenic roads. First major stop: Bow Lake viewpoint (free) with reflections of Crowfoot Glacier (~40 min from Banff).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Peyto Lake Viewpoint – a short 1.5 km walk up to the famous wolf-shaped turquoise lake overlook, arguably the most photogenic view in the Canadian Rockies (free with Parks pass). Then drive to the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre (~2.5 hrs from Banff) to view the Athabasca Glacier from the free viewpoint platform. Skip the paid glacier walk to stay on budget. Return south along the Parkway, stopping at Sunwapta Falls (~$0, roadside stop) on the way back.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Banff by 6:30–7:00 PM. Quiet evening – walk to Vermilion Lakes (10-min drive or 30-min bike ride from town) for spectacular mountain reflections and wildlife at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered packed breakfast to eat in the car – muffins, fruit, and a thermos of coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch eaten at Peyto Lake or Bow Lake shore – sandwiches, trail mix, and snacks.
meals.dinner: Melissa's Missteak (Banff) – a Banff institution since 1972, known for hearty comfort food at reasonable prices; budget ~$18–$24 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Fill up the gas tank in Banff before leaving – fuel is cheaper in town than along the Parkway. The full Icefields Parkway to Jasper is ~230 km one-way; this day covers roughly the southern half (to the Columbia Icefield and back), about 280 km total round-trip. Start early to maximize daylight and avoid afternoon crowds at Peyto Lake.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – sunrise walk along the Bow River Trail from the hotel (flat, easy, free). Pack up luggage and check out of Banff Mountain Lodge. Visit the Banff Farmers' Market if running on a weekend morning (local crafts and produce – great for last-minute souvenirs on a budget).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last stop before departing: hike or walk up to the Cave and Basin National Historic Site (~$5–$8 CAD entry) – the birthplace of Canada's national parks system, with warm sulphur springs and fascinating history. Then drive or shuttle back to Calgary Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary. Reflect on an incredible week in the Canadian Rockies!

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast at the lodge – use up remaining groceries to avoid waste.
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich and coffee from Wild Flour Bakery (Banff) – one of the best bakeries in town, great value; budget ~$10–$14 CAD.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight, depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Book the return Brewster/On It shuttle to Calgary Airport in advance (~$25–$30 CAD). Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the shuttle ride plus airport check-in. The Cave and Basin is a quick but meaningful visit – budget 1–1.5 hours. Total estimated trip budget (excluding flights and park pass): ~$400–$550 CAD for 6 days covering accommodation, food, transport, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary International Airport at 14:00, collect luggage and pick up a rental car (recommended for the trip). Drive the scenic 1.5-hour Trans-Canada Highway route to Banff (~140 km). Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along Banff Avenue to get oriented — browse local shops and enjoy the mountain town atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Bow River Trail on foot for a relaxed 30-minute walk near the hotel to shake off travel fatigue and take in the stunning mountain backdrop at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Grab something at the airport before or during the flight
meals.lunch: Airport or roadside stop en route — Tim Hortons on the Trans-Canada is a classic Canadian option
meals.dinner: Elk & Oarsman Restaurant on Banff Avenue — a mid-range Banff staple with hearty Canadian comfort food, burgers, and local craft beer; budget ~$30–45 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a Parks Canada day pass or annual Discovery Pass at the park gate on entry — required for all stops within Banff National Park. Confirm rental car booking in advance. Stock up on snacks and water at Safeway or IGA on Banff Avenue for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Early start — depart hotel by 7:00 AM to beat the crowds at Moraine Lake (parking fills by 7:30 AM in peak summer; alternatively use the Parks Canada shuttle from the Banff Gondola base or Lake Louise overflow lot). Complete the Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek: hike the short but rewarding Rockpile Trail (20 min, stunning panoramic view of the lake and ten soaring peaks) followed by the full Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return, ~1 hour, easy terrain along the impossibly blue glacial lake).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 15 minutes to Lake Louise. Walk the iconic Lake Louise Shoreline Hike — follow the flat lakeshore trail (4 km return) with views of the Victoria Glacier, then continue up to the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (14 km return, ~4–5 hours total, moderate difficulty with 365 m elevation gain). Enjoy a well-earned tea and snack at the historic teahouse perched above the glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff for a relaxed evening. Stroll through Central Park along the Bow River and enjoy the sunset over Mount Rundle.

meals.breakfast: Pack a hearty breakfast from the hotel or grab a quick bite at Whitebark Cafe in Banff before departing — excellent coffee and breakfast wraps
meals.lunch: Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse — soups, sandwiches, and baked goods in a magical alpine setting; cash only, ~$15–20 CAD; pack backup snacks
meals.dinner: Coyotes Southwestern Grill on Banff Avenue — fresh, flavourful southwestern cuisine with vegetarian-friendly options; ~$25–40 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: This is the most demanding day — wear sturdy hiking boots, bring trekking poles if available, and carry at least 2L of water per person. Layers are essential as temperatures drop near the glaciers. The Moraine Lake road may require a shuttle reservation — book via the Parks Canada reservation system well in advance. Start as early as possible.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike — depart by 8:30 AM for the 25-minute drive from Banff. Follow the dramatic canyon catwalk bolted into limestone cliffs to the Lower Falls (2.4 km return, easy, ~45 min) and then continue to the Upper Falls (5.4 km return, easy-moderate, ~2 hours total). Optional extension to the Ink Pots (11.6 km return, moderate) — seven cold mineral springs in a meadow with mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff for a relaxed afternoon. Visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$18 CAD entry) — a perfect recovery soak with views of Mount Rundle. Afterward, explore the Banff Park Museum National Historic Site on Banff Avenue (free entry with Parks Pass), a fascinating Victorian-era natural history museum.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset walk up Tunnel Mountain Trail (4.8 km return, moderate, ~1.5 hours) — one of the most accessible hikes near town with sweeping views of the Bow Valley, Hoodoos, and Mount Rundle.

meals.breakfast: Tooloulou's on Caribou Street — beloved local breakfast spot with generous portions; ~$15–20 CAD; arrive early as it fills up quickly
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from Banff Ave Brewing or grab sandwiches from Nourish Bistro to eat at the canyon or Ink Pots meadow
meals.dinner: Banff Ave Brewing Co. — lively brewpub atmosphere with wood-fired pizza, burgers, and house-brewed craft beer; ~$25–40 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon can get very busy mid-morning — an early start is strongly recommended. The catwalk can be slippery; wear grippy footwear. The hot springs are a wonderful recovery option after two big hiking days. Tunnel Mountain at sunset is a highlight not to miss.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive — depart Banff by 8:00 AM and head north on Highway 93, one of the world's most scenic roads. First major stop: Bow Lake (96 km from Banff) — a stunning glacial lake with a short shoreline walk. Continue to Peyto Lake Viewpoint (a short 800 m walk to the famous wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake, one of the most photographed views in Canada). Spend time at each stop soaking in the scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to the Columbia Icefield area (~230 km from Banff). Stop at the Athabasca Glacier viewpoint for a walk to the glacier toe on the free public path (do not venture onto the ice without a guide). Visit the Icefield Centre for exhibits on the glacier. Begin the return drive south, stopping at Sunwapta Falls (a powerful double waterfall) and Mistaya Canyon (a short 1 km walk to a dramatic limestone canyon) on the way back.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Banff by 7:00–8:00 PM. Enjoy a well-deserved relaxed dinner and an early night.

meals.breakfast: Grab a packed breakfast or visit Wild Flour Bakery on Bear Street before departing — excellent pastries and coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial lunch and snacks for the road — there are limited dining options on the Parkway. The Num-Ti-Jah Lodge at Bow Lake has a restaurant if you prefer a sit-down option (~$20–30 CAD)
meals.dinner: The Bison Restaurant & Terrace on Bear Street — locally sourced Canadian cuisine in a warm, rustic setting; ~$35–55 CAD per person; a slight splurge worth it after a big day

day_by_day.notes: Fill up the gas tank before leaving Banff — there are very few fuel stations on the Icefields Parkway. This is a full driving day (~460 km round trip) so an early departure is essential. A wildlife-spotting checklist adds fun — bears, elk, bighorn sheep, and mountain goats are commonly seen along the Parkway. Bring binoculars if available.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk — ride the Banff Gondola (~$65 CAD per person) to the summit of Sulphur Mountain at 2,281 metres. Walk the 1 km Summit Boardwalk along the ridge connecting to Sanson Peak with panoramic 360° views of six mountain ranges. Visit the restored Cosmic Ray Station National Historic Site at the summit. Allow 2–3 hours total.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and spend the afternoon exploring downtown Banff at a relaxed pace. Visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (excellent local art, history, and photography; ~$10 CAD entry). Browse the galleries and boutiques on Bear Street. Optional: rent a canoe or kayak on the Bow River (~$50 CAD/hour) for a peaceful paddle with mountain reflections.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the Vermilion Lakes — drive 5 minutes west of Banff to this iconic wetland area with mirror-like reflections of Mount Rundle. A favourite spot for wildlife (beavers, herons, elk) and photographers. Perfect way to spend the second-to-last evening.

meals.breakfast: Melissa's MistSteak on Lynx Street — a Banff institution for 40+ years; hearty breakfasts with big portions; ~$15–25 CAD
meals.lunch: Saltlik Steakhouse has a casual lunch menu, or try Aardvark Pizza for a quick and popular local slice; ~$15–20 CAD
meals.dinner: Block Kitchen & Bar on Banff Avenue — modern Canadian small plates and shared dishes in a stylish setting; great for a fun, social evening meal; ~$30–45 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: The Banff Gondola can be booked online in advance to avoid queues — recommended in peak July season. Alternatively, the fit and adventurous can hike up Sulphur Mountain (9.6 km return, moderate-strenuous, ~3 hours) and ride the gondola down for free. Vermilion Lakes is best visited 30–60 minutes before sunset for the best light and wildlife activity.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a relaxed breakfast and a last walk through Banff townsite. Visit the Cave and Basin National Historic Site (the birthplace of Canada's national park system; ~$8 CAD entry, 1–2 hours) — fascinating boardwalk trails around the thermal sulphur springs and interpretive exhibits on the park's history. A meaningful and low-key final activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge (standard checkout 11:00 AM — request late checkout if needed). Drive back to Calgary Airport (~1.5 hours), allowing plenty of time to return the rental car and clear security. Enjoy a final coffee or souvenir shopping on Banff Avenue before departing if time allows.

meals.breakfast: Whitebark Cafe — a perfect final Banff breakfast with excellent espresso drinks and fresh pastries in a cozy mountain setting; ~$12–18 CAD
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and satisfying lunch at Evelyn's Coffee Bar on Banff Avenue or pack snacks for the drive to Calgary
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Calgary International — OEB Breakfast Co. or Earls Kitchen + Bar in the terminal are solid options for a final Canadian meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight departure time to account for the drive, car return, and airport security. Pick up any last souvenirs — local maple syrup, Parks Canada pins, or Rocky Mountain chocolate are popular choices. Consider a final stop at Two Jack Lake (10 min from Banff) on the way out for a last iconic mountain reflection photo.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight AC arrives at 14:00. Travel time from Calgary International Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge is approximately 1.5 hours by private transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Calgary Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge. Check in, unpack, and settle into your suite. Take a leisurely stroll along Banff Avenue to get acquainted with the town, browse boutique shops, and soak in the stunning mountain backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed first evening in Banff. Visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs for a soothing soak in mineral-rich thermal waters at 2,190 metres elevation — the perfect way to recover from travel. Return to the lodge for a premium welcome dinner.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast on the plane or at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: Light refreshments during transfer — pre-arrange a gourmet snack hamper through the lodge concierge.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Maple Leaf Restaurant, Banff — a celebrated fine-dining destination known for Canadian cuisine including Alberta beef tenderloin and wild Pacific salmon, with an award-winning Canadian wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private luxury vehicle transfer (e.g., Brewster Express or a private car service) in advance. Ask the lodge concierge to pre-book the Banff Upper Hot Springs entry and reserve dinner. Tip: stay hydrated upon arrival as Banff sits at 1,383 metres elevation.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike — Depart early (7:00 AM) with a private guided transfer to Lake Louise (45 minutes from Banff). Walk the iconic turquoise shoreline and continue up the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail to the historic teahouse at 2,135 metres. The round trip is approximately 13.8 km with 365 m elevation gain. A private naturalist guide will narrate the geology, glacial history, and alpine flora along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending from the teahouse, enjoy lunch at the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise. Spend the afternoon exploring the lakeshore at a relaxed pace, optionally renting a premium canoe on the impossibly turquoise waters for a closer look at Victoria Glacier. Return to Banff Mountain Lodge by private transfer by 5:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Freshen up at the lodge, then enjoy a sunset cocktail on the terrace before heading to dinner. If energy allows, take a short evening walk along the Bow River Trail near the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge or at the lodge restaurant before departure — fuel up well for the hike.
meals.lunch: Afternoon tea and light lunch at the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (cash only, rustic alpine charm) or a full sit-down lunch at the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise's Lakeview Lounge upon return.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eden Restaurant at the Rimrock Resort Hotel — Banff's only CAA/AAA Five Diamond restaurant, offering French-inspired contemporary cuisine with panoramic mountain views. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Book private guide and transport through the lodge concierge well in advance. Start early to beat crowds at Lake Louise — this is one of Canada's most visited sites. Wear layered clothing as temperatures at elevation can be 5–8°C cooler than town. Trekking poles recommended for the Plain of Six Glaciers ascent.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake — Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek — Private transfer departs at 6:30 AM (access to Moraine Lake requires early arrival or a reserved shuttle; private vehicles may be restricted — confirm current Parks Canada access policy). Hike the Rockpile Trail for the world-famous Valley of the Ten Peaks panorama, then continue along the Lakeshore Trail (5.8 km round trip). A private guide will share the cultural significance of this sacred Stoney Nakoda landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff by 1:00 PM. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the lodge — use the spa, pool, or simply relax on your private balcony with mountain views. Optional: visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies for a curated cultural experience of the region's art and history.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset hike or walk along Tunnel Mountain Trail (2.7 km loop, easy) for sweeping panoramic views of the Bow Valley and Banff townsite at golden hour — spectacular in summer light.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast prepared by the lodge or a packed gourmet breakfast box arranged by concierge — eaten en route or at the lake.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Moraine Lake — request a premium gourmet picnic hamper from the lodge (charcuterie, artisan cheeses, smoked salmon, sparkling water, and local treats).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Saltlik Steakhouse, Banff — a premium steakhouse renowned for AAA Alberta prime beef, dry-aged cuts, and an extensive bourbon and wine selection in an upscale yet relaxed atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake road access is strictly managed by Parks Canada — confirm the latest reservation or shuttle system before the trip. Book the Parks Canada shuttle or private permitted vehicle well in advance. Moraine Lake is even more stunning in early morning light. Bring bear spray (available to rent/purchase in Banff) — this is active wildlife habitat.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike — Private guided transfer to Johnston Canyon (25 minutes from Banff). Walk the dramatic catwalk trail bolted into limestone cliffs above the rushing creek. Visit the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km round trip), and optionally continue to the Ink Pots — seven cold mineral springs in a stunning alpine meadow (11 km round trip total). The guide will explain the canyon's karst geology and local wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon on a curated wildlife safari by private 4x4 along the Bow Valley Parkway (Highway 1A) — a premier wildlife corridor where elk, deer, black bears, wolves, and bighorn sheep are frequently spotted. A professional wildlife guide will accompany the drive.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a premium spa treatment at the lodge or a local luxury spa (e.g., Willow Stream Spa at the Fairmont Banff Springs). End the day with a sophisticated dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at the lodge restaurant before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Baker Creek by Basecamp — a charming, upscale bistro along the Bow Valley Parkway, known for locally sourced Canadian comfort cuisine in a cozy log-cabin setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bison Restaurant & Terrace, Banff — a beloved farm-to-table restaurant celebrating Rocky Mountain ingredients: bison short rib, foraged mushrooms, Alberta lamb, and local craft cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon is popular — arriving early (before 9:00 AM) ensures a quieter experience. The Ink Pots extension adds approximately 2 hours but is highly recommended for the surreal turquoise springs. The Bow Valley Parkway wildlife drive is best in late afternoon when animals are most active. Book spa treatments in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive & Peyto Lake Viewpoint — Depart at 8:00 AM in a private luxury vehicle with a knowledgeable driver-guide. Drive north along the legendary Icefields Parkway (Highway 93), consistently ranked among the world's most scenic roads. Stop at Bow Lake (short walk to the lakeshore), then ascend to the Peyto Lake Viewpoint — a wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake in the Mistaya Valley, one of the most photographed landscapes in Canada.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to the Columbia Icefield — the largest non-polar icefield in North America. Board the Pursuit Ice Explorer for a guided excursion onto the Athabasca Glacier. Visit the Glacier Skywalk, a glass-floored observation platform suspended 280 metres above the Sunwapta Valley. Begin the scenic return drive south along the Parkway, stopping at Sunwapta Falls and Athabasca Falls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by 6:30–7:00 PM. Celebrate the penultimate evening with a premium cocktail at the Sky Bistro (accessible by gondola) or at the lodge lounge, followed by a special dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early full breakfast at the lodge before departure.
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch hamper from the lodge, enjoyed at a scenic pullout along the Icefields Parkway — perhaps at Bow Lake with the Crowfoot Glacier as a backdrop.
meals.dinner: Farewell-eve dinner at the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel's 1888 Chop House — an iconic fine-dining experience inside the legendary castle hotel, featuring prime Alberta beef, fresh seafood, and an exceptional wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: The full Icefields Parkway round trip is approximately 430 km — a long but extraordinary day. Pre-book the Pursuit Ice Explorer and Glacier Skywalk tickets. Bring an extra layer as the Athabasca Glacier is significantly colder (often near 0°C on the ice). This is the longest day of the itinerary — a packed gourmet lunch is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk — A perfect final morning activity. Board the Banff Gondola (a short drive from the lodge) and ascend to the summit of Sulphur Mountain at 2,281 metres. Walk the 1-km summit boardwalk to Sanson's Peak for 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges, the Bow Valley, and the town of Banff far below. A premium gondola experience includes access to the interpretive centre and rooftop terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend by mid-morning and return to the lodge for a final lunch and checkout. Pack, settle any outstanding lodge services, and arrange private luxury transfer back to Calgary International Airport (departing Banff no later than 1:30 PM to allow ample time for check-in). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Bow Valley one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary International Airport. If the flight departs late evening, enjoy a final dinner at a premium Calgary restaurant such as CHARCUT Roast House or River Café on Prince's Island Park.

meals.breakfast: Final full gourmet breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge — savour the mountain views one last time.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at Sky Bistro at the top of the Banff Gondola (book a window table) — offering elevated Canadian cuisine with the most dramatic views in Banff.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Calgary Airport's premium lounge or a fine restaurant near the airport if the departure schedule allows — coordinate with the concierge based on final flight details.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — request a late checkout (12:00–1:00 PM) through the concierge to allow time after the gondola. The gondola opens at 8:00 AM in summer. Tip: purchase any final Canadian Rocky Mountain souvenirs in Banff town before heading to the gondola. Confirm private transfer timing the evening before to avoid any last-minute stress.
